issues.legal_issue: An amount of agricultural income-tax may be deducted in determining compensation only when it has been finally assessed, not while the assessment remains under appeal.
material_facts: Compensation was being assessed under a statutory scheme that allowed deduction for agricultural income-tax paid or payable for the previous agricultural year.
The recipients appealed the tax assessment, and the appellate authority set it aside and remanded the matter for a fresh assessment.
The State argued that the amount assessed by the first authority had to be used despite the pending appeal.
issues.conclusion: The tax amount to be taken into account is the amount finally assessed, not an amount that remains under appeal; the compensation assessment was to be redetermined in light of the eventual tax assessment.
issues.legal_principle: Section 44(b) of the U.P. Zamindari Abolition and Land Reforms Act, 1950, read with Rules 37(A) and 38, contemplates deduction of agricultural income-tax that has been finally assessed. Rule 38's requirement to report tax assessed does not make an assessment under appeal conclusive for compensation purposes.

predicates.compensation_assessment_case: A compensation assessment is being made under a scheme that permits a deduction for agricultural income-tax paid or payable for a previous year.
predicates.agricultural_tax_assessment_under_appeal: The relevant agricultural income-tax assessment remains under appeal rather than being final.

issues.definition: When compensation is being assessed and the relevant agricultural tax assessment remains under appeal, only tax that has been finally assessed is counted.

issues.legal_issue: Accepting compensation under protest and without prejudice does not make the compensation determination final or estop a recipient from challenging it.
material_facts: The recipients did not file objections to the compensation assessed and accepted the compensation paid under protest and without prejudice.
Government circulars directed compensation officers to await the outcome of references and appeals against the agricultural tax assessments before finalising compensation.
The State argued that the lack of objections and acceptance of payment made the compensation final and barred a challenge.
issues.conclusion: The compensation had not become final, and its acceptance under protest and without prejudice did not estop the recipients from challenging it.
issues.legal_principle: A payment accepted under protest and without prejudice is not an unconditional acceptance that bars a challenge. Where government circulars direct officers to await related tax proceedings, the compensation is not final while those proceedings remain unresolved.

predicates.compensation_assessment_case: A compensation assessment is being made while a related agricultural tax assessment may affect the amount.
predicates.government_directed_wait_for_tax_appeals: The government directed compensation officers to wait for the outcome of related tax references or appeals before finalising compensation.
predicates.compensation_accepted_under_protest: The recipient accepted the compensation payment expressly under protest and without prejudice.

issues.definition: If compensation is being assessed, the government directed officers to await related tax appeals, and the recipient accepted payment conditionally, that acceptance does not make the compensation final or bar a challenge.
